cases.name: built-in worked example
stdout: (no config - demo: Example Co., a fictional company, with invented numbers)
MQLs to SQLs converted at 24.0% against 32.0% in Q2 2026. At the baseline rate, with every other stage as it is, this period would have had 9.3 more wins ($167,329).
- Each stage's figure holds the other stages at this period's rates, so the figures do not add up to the total change.
- In AAJ's view, fix the named leak before adding volume at the top: more volume through a stage that is below baseline buys fewer wins per unit of spend than it did at baseline.
- The noise check uses 95% (two-sided) and needs at least 5 conversions and 5 non-conversions in each period; those cut-offs are AAJ's choice.

NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook of Statistical Methods, "7.3.3. How can we determine whether two processes produce the same proportion of defectives?": https://www.itl.nist.gov/div898/handbook/prc/section3/prc33.htm

cases.name: no baseline names no leak
stdout: No leak can be named without a baseline. Raw drop-off cannot name one: each stage's rate has its own scale, and a 10% relative lift at any stage gives the same 10% more wins. Add last period's counts ("prior") or your target rates ("targets") to see which stage cost you wins.

cases.name: targets with a named source, one stage without a target
stdout: SQLs to Opportunities converted at 44.4% against your target of 50.0% (2026 plan). At the baseline rate, with every other stage as it is, this period would have had 1.1 more wins ($27,000). The change may be noise (not significant at 95%): confirm it next period before acting.
- No target for oppsToWins: that stage is shown but not judged, so it cannot be named as the leak.
- In AAJ's view, fix the named leak before adding volume at the top: more volume through a stage that is below baseline buys fewer wins per unit of spend than it did at baseline.
- The noise check uses 95% (two-sided) and needs the stage count times the target, and times one minus the target, to be at least 5 (NIST 7.2.4); the 95% level is AAJ's choice.
NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook of Statistical Methods, "7.2.4. Does the proportion of defectives meet requirements?": https://www.itl.nist.gov/div898/handbook/prc/section2/prc24.htm
